newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong debates role of politics in handover year. [CORRECTED 12:06 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong debates role of politics in handover year. [CORRECTED 12:06 GMT]

text.p: The call for a less politicised society by Hong Kong's future leader was both challenged and echoed on Sunday as the British colony heads toward its transition into a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China.

Local newspapers were divided in their response to chief-executive designate Tung Chee-hwa's Lunar New Year message to the territory on Friday to focus less on politics after it reverts to Chinese rule from July 1.
The English-language South China Morning Post said politics was the way in which people participated in the development of their society.
"Social welfare and housing policy involve politics," the Post said in its editorial.

"Politics need not mean a divided society. On the contrary, an absence of free debate and of a public popular involvement which politics brings risks undermining cohesion as we move into this new era of our history," it said.

Tung said in his message: "I really hope that after the handover on July 1, 1997, that our society will not be as politicised and we can focus more on livelihood issues such as housing, education and welfare," he said.
Tung urged Hong Kong people to respect Chinese traditions that stress harmony, compassion and family values.

"Chinese tradition emphasises the 'Golden Mean', just as Tung Chee-hwa said in his New Year message, stressing family values and avoiding extremes," the Hong Kong Daily News said in its editorial on Sunday.
"All sectors and political parties should act according to the Golden Mean ... strengthening social stability for a smooth transition and laying a sound foundation for the SAR," it said.

"Less politicisation of society and more focusing of efforts on solving the problems of housing, education and the elderly, we trust these hopes are felt not only by Tung Chee-hwa but are shared by many Hong Kong people," the Sing Tao Daily said.

Some newspapers also urged their readers to recall the more traditional virtues of the ox -- the animal in the Chinese zodiac symbolising this lunar year -- such as strength, sincerity, meekness and persistence.

A politicised Hong Kong is a relatively recent phenomenon. The territory's legislature chosen in September 1995 was the first to be fully-elected in over 150 years of British colonial rule. The council was fully appointed as recently as mid-1985, after which it was composed of a mix of elected and appointed members. (Corrects to make clear that the council was not fully appointed all the way up to 1995)
Tung's New Year message came amid increasing political tension in the territory after China's recent plan to roll back some civil rights after the handover.
The move triggered strong protests in Hong Kong and prompted the international community to lodge official protests with China.
